**Run:** S&P 500 price index (daily, 1990-01-02 to 2022-12-28; from the dataset bundled in the
`skfolio` package, originally Yahoo ^GSPC) + CBOE VIX daily (datahub `finance-vix`).
69 quarterly origins 2004-12-31 to 2021-12-31, full ensemble refit at each one (10,000 MC paths).
Run in a sandbox where FRED, Finnhub and Yahoo were unreachable, so it uses **price + VIX features
only**: no macro, rates, news or calendar inputs. No dividends. The 2022Q4 target is unscored
(data ends Dec 28). The model was written before this backtest and not tuned on it.

# Walk-forward backtest

Origins scored: 69 (skipped: 0).  
Pinball skill vs baseline: +4.0%  
90% CI of mean loss difference (model - baseline, per origin): [-0.00457, +0.00132]

## Verdict

- The ensemble does NOT reliably beat the naive baseline: skill +4.0%, but the 90% CI of the loss difference [-0.00457, +0.00132] includes zero.
- Model coverage 78% is within 70-90% of the 80% target (baseline 79%).
- Directional hit rate 73% vs baseline 75% (the baseline almost always says 'up', so it scores the share of up periods).
- Drawdown-probability Brier 0.254 vs baseline 0.228 (worse).
- 2008 GFC: model coverage 38%, below P10 62%; pinball 0.0806 vs baseline 0.0971.
- 2020 COVID: model coverage 62%, below P10 31%; pinball 0.0426 vs baseline 0.0444.
- 2022 rate shock: model coverage 44%, below P10 56%; pinball 0.0628 vs baseline 0.0528.
